title: Interteam Dependency Simulation & Gamified Playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a repeatable, low-friction program + artifact set to surface, rehearse, and reduce cross-team roadmap dependencies. The core product is a Dependency Simulation Kit: scenario templates, a gamified scoring rubric, a small web UI for running tabletop exercises, and Linear automation recipes that convert discovered blockers into prioritized follow-ups. The aim is to reduce hidden coupling, shorten mitigation lead time, and improve interlock quality for quarterly OKR cutovers.
objectives: Create a canonical 'dependency story' library covering common multi-team cuts (runtime rollout, dedicated capacity onboarding, private deployment upgrades, console schema changes)
Produce 12 scenario templates that can be executed in a 60-minute workshop
Deliver an automated Linear workflow that transforms exercise findings into ticket seeds with priority recommendations
Measure improvement in time-to-mitigate and unplanned blocker count for the next cycle
deliverables: Simulation web UI prototype for running exercises (internal GitHub repo)
Linear automation recipes and ticket templates
Quarterly scoreboard dashboard in Console showing dependency heat and mitigation velocity
success_metrics: Reduce mean time-to-mitigate cross-team blockers from 18 days to <=10 days within two quarters
Increase percent of roadmap deps with assigned owners at planning gate from 62% to 90%
Run 8 simulation workshops in Q2 with at least one representative from Eng/Design/Security/Infra per workshop
acceptance_criteria: Confluence Dependency Storybook published with 12 unique scenarios and acceptance criteria for each
Simulation UI prototype deployed to staging and usable by facilitators (login + create/run/session export)
Linear automation created: exercise -> ticket seeds with suggested priority and owner hints
Pilot workshops executed with at least 3 teams and post-workshop action rate >= 75% within 7 days
work_plan: Week 1: Discovery interviews with Eng/Design/Security/Infra stewards to collect common failure modes
Week 2: Draft 12 scenario templates and rubric; validate with two partner squads
Week 3: Build minimal Simulation UI prototype (session creation, timer, scoring, export)
Week 4: Implement Linear automation templates and ticket seeding rules; wire to follow-up cadence
Week 5: Pilot two workshops, iterate on playbook and templates
Week 6: Build Console scoreboard query and dashboard; prepare roll-out kit
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff — interviewed runtime, console, and dedicated teams. Collected 18 real dependency anecdotes. Decided to prioritize deployment upgrade and schema change scenarios.
2026-02-18: Design completed first pass of 4 scenario cards. Security recommends adding a compliance-verification step for Private deployment scenarios.
2026-02-22: Eng spike shows linear automation can create ticket seeds using the API with labels and suggested owners. Prototype script linked in repo.
2026-02-25: Pilot workshop scheduled with Infra and Runtime on 2026-03-08. Slack channel #dep-sim created for coordination.
2026-03-01: MVP Simulation UI prototype deployed to staging; basic scoring and export works. Need UX polish and facilitator guide writeup.
decisions: Keep simulation UI minimal for MVP — focus on facilitator workflow and export into Linear rather than a full participant-facing app
Scoring rubric will weight customer-impact and unblock-time-to-ship higher than implementation-complexity to bias mitigation effort toward customer-facing risk
Dependency story format standard: summary, impacted teams, API/schema/contracts, rollout triggers, mitigation playbook, owner suggestions, and acceptance criteria
risks_mitigation: Risk: Teams may treat the simulation as a checkbox. Mitigation: require at least one concrete ticket seed per workshop and ask executive sponsor to review top-3 actions
Risk: Automation mis-assigns owners. Mitigation: automation suggests owners but requires human confirmation before ticket creation
Risk: Workshop fatigue. Mitigation: keep workshops to 60 minutes, provide pre-read and one facilitator per session
rollout_plan: Month 1: Pilot with Runtime + Dedicated + Console squads (2 workshops)
Month 2: Iterate on templates and automation based on pilot feedback; publish Storybook
Month 3: Expand to 6 additional teams; integrate scoreboard into Console and present at quarterly planning
Ongoing: Quarterly simulation week before each major roadmap cutover
